tools.name: memory_entity
tools.description: Fetch a single entity (person, company, or deal) and its known facts by id. Ends with a revision; send it back as ifRevision to skip an answer you already hold. Access-scoped and audited.

tools.name: memory_version
tools.description: Fetch one stored version of a fact or a rule by its id — the id a change notice gives you when another agent's write superseded yours, or when your own write lost a race. tools.name: memory_ingest
tools.description: Store a fact, note or decision in Willder's business memory (needs a token with memory.write). memory_query reads it, and other agents' memory_changes lists it, as soon as the call returns. Only content and name are needed; leave the other arguments out unless you need what one describes.

tools.name: fact_link_source
tools.description: Record that a stored fact/decision came from a specific PR, commit, or file, so it can later be flagged if that source changes. tools.name: get_my_brief
tools.description: Fetch a generated brief (Handoff/Architecture/QA agent output) for this org. Defaults to the most recent brief within your token's own scope if no id is given.

tools.name: memory_stale
tools.description: Records in a scope (briefs, derived records) whose cited or source fact has been replaced, or was changed or removed after they were built, most depended-on first. Read-only; access-scoped and audited.

tools.name: memory_changes
tools.description: List memory changes another agent or person made, newest last. Your own writes are never listed: you already know them, and a memory_ingest is readable by the time the call returns, so read it back with memory_query instead. tools.name: contact_search
tools.description: Search this org's contacts by name/email substring. Requires a capability token with memory.read permission covering the org root.

tools.name: contact_read
tools.description: Fetch a single contact by id. Requires a capability token with memory.read permission covering the org root.

tools.name: contact_upsert
tools.description: Create a new contact or update an existing one (by contactId or by matching email). Requires a capability token with memory.write permission covering the org root. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fact_link_source, contact_search · Private data: memory_ingest, fact_link_source, get_my_brief, memory_stale, memory_note, contact_search, contact_read, contact_upsert, send_feedback · Public sink: memory_query, memory_entity, fact_link_source, memory_note, contact_search, contact_upsert, send_feedback · Destructive: send_feedback.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fact_link_source, contact_search · Private data: memory_ingest, fact_link_source, get_my_brief, memory_stale, memory_note, contact_search, contact_read, contact_upsert, send_feedback · Public sink: memory_query, memory_entity, fact_link_source, memory_note, contact_search, contact_upsert, send_feedback · Destructive: send_feedback

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
